paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this chapter. Nehemiah gets pulled from every side: the same invite over and over, a letter, a "prophet" with a scary warning. Every one of them was built to get him off the wall. His answer to the first one tells you everything: "I am doing a great work and cannot come down" (Nehemiah 6:3).

Now watch what he does when the pressure gets personal. The enemies wanted him to hide in the temple and sin, so they could give him "a bad name" (Nehemiah 6:13), but Nehemiah says, "Should a man like me run away?" (Nehemiah 6:11), and he realized God had not sent that man (Nehemiah 6:12). And when the letters tried to frighten everybody, he prayed, "But now, my God, strengthen my hands" (Nehemiah 6:9). That's the move, baker: when the fear shows up, hand it to God and keep working.

And look how it ends. The wall was completed in fifty-two days (Nehemiah 6:15), and the surrounding nations "realized that this task had been accomplished by our God" (Nehemiah 6:16). The enemies never stopped the work, but they sure kept trying, right up to the last verse (Nehemiah 6:19). So whatever God has put in your hands this week, don't let a loud voice talk you down off your wall. Stay on it, ask Him to strengthen your hands, and I'll be right here keeping the oven warm.
